EmoryHacks × Chert

[![Chert](/_next/image?url=%2Fchert-lockup.png&w=384&q=75&REDACTED)](/)[API docs](https://docs.trychert.com/introduction)

![](/_next/image?url=%2Frenewal%2Feveryday.webp&w=3840&q=75&REDACTED)

Chert × EmoryHacks

Emory Hacks
===========

Best Use of FaceTime
--------------------

Chert puts AI agents in iMessage and FaceTime. Build one that’s more useful when it can see.

Start building
--------------

Copy prompt

1.  **Copy** the prompt below.
2.  **Paste** it into Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. No forms, about 5 minutes.
3.  That’s it. You’re on Chert with **a free Chert line for 48 hours**.

`Connect my agent to Chert so I can FaceTime it. Follow https://app.trychert.com/skills.md`

**$400**1st place

Y**1st place team gets guaranteed interviews**for our _FDE and SWE intern_ roles. We’re currently expanding our team and actively hiring.

Friday, 6–7 PM**Chert workshop**Learn to build on Chert. Free shirts.

[Join the Discord](https://discord.gg/MNnPMrmHe)

Need ideas? Find **Stanley** at the help desk.

9:41●●●

![](/_next/image?url=%2Fchert-mark.png&w=48&q=75&REDACTED)Chert

iMessage

Hey EmoryHacks! I’m Chert. Text me anything about the FaceTime track.

Prizes, rules, what to bring, an idea to build, or how to reach the team.

Give me a project ideaWhat are the prizes?What do we need to bring?Is it free?How is it judged?What does the winner get?Talk to the Chert team

Ask Chert a question

[Rules, judging and ideas](#challenge)

What Chert does

We put AI agents in iMessage and FaceTime.
------------------------------------------

We treat FaceTime as a channel for realtime video. Your agent sees the caller’s camera live, sends video back, and can call people when something comes up.

*   Sees the caller’s video live
*   Sends video back
*   Group FaceTime calls
*   Places and answers calls
*   Texts over iMessage

It can be a character you talk to, or no character at all. Build an agent that gets more useful the moment it can see.

Backed by **Y Combinator (P26)**, **OpenAI**, **Z Fellows** and angels.

Voice only

Uh, which cable?

On FaceTime

blue, 2nd

“The blue cable, second from the left.”

A demo we love

ClawdTime: your coding agent FaceTimes you.
-------------------------------------------

You step away from your laptop. Claude Code or Codex hits a decision. Your phone rings. You answer, say “use the blue heading,” and the agent keeps working on your computer.

It’s your computer, from anywhere, over a FaceTime call. Built on Chert. This is the kind of build we want to see.

[See ClawdTime](https://www.clawdtime.com)

✳**Claude Code**ClawdTime · 0:42Mac screen

localhost:3000

Give your agent eyes.

Use the blue heading.

Done. Want me to push it?

To qualify
----------

*   **Build on Chert’s FaceTime API**iMessage is optional, but encouraged.
*   **Bring an iPhone**At least one per team.
*   **Call during your demo**Your agent makes or takes a FaceTime call.

When you submit on Devpost, select “Best Use of FaceTime (Chert)”.

How it’s judged
---------------

*   **Fresh use of FaceTime video**It uses what it sees in a way we haven’t seen.Weight 2×
*   **Wow factor**People stop and say “wait, how did you do that?”Weight 1×
*   **Usefulness**It solves a real problem people want solved.Weight 1×

S

**Live demo, judged in person by Stanley Yang from Chert.**Show it working on a real FaceTime call.

Template ideas
--------------

**Your own idea wins.**The best projects are ones we haven’t seen. Use these only as a starting point, and if you build on one, put a real spin on it. “Fresh use of FaceTime video” counts double in judging.

*   Agents
    
    ### Your background agent calls you
    
    A long-running coding or ops agent hits a decision, places a FaceTime call, shows you the diff, logs or chart as its video, takes your spoken answer, and resumes.
    
    Under the hood
    
    1.  Agent hook fires on blocker
    2.  Chert places the call
    3.  Render terminal or diff to video frames
    4.  Speech to text → tool call → resume
    
    **Your spin:** What else runs unattended? Training runs, deploys, scrapers, trading sims.
    
*   Hardware
    
    ### Breadboard bring-up copilot
    
    Point your camera at a breadboard or PCB. The agent reads the parts and wire colors, checks them against your schematic, and sends back an annotated frame of what’s wrong.
    
    Under the hood
    
    1.  Sample frames at 1–2 fps
    2.  Vision model + part detection
    3.  Diff against netlist or KiCad export
    4.  Draw boxes, stream the frame back
    
    **Your spin:** Swap the schematic for a 3D-printer, a robot arm or a car engine bay.
    
*   Group calls
    
    ### Group-call game master
    
    Everyone joins one group FaceTime. The agent watches the table, tracks the board state, rules on disputes, and shows a live scoreboard as its video.
    
    Under the hood
    
    1.  Group call with every player
    2.  Board-state model per frame
    3.  Game state machine + rules engine
    4.  Render scoreboard as outgoing video
    
    **Your spin:** Chess, poker, a D&D table, a sports drill, a study-group quiz.
    
*   Procedures
    
    ### Step-by-step verifier
    
    The agent turns a procedure into a step graph and won’t advance until it sees each step done correctly on camera. Skip one and it calls you back.
    
    Under the hood
    
    1.  Parse the doc into a step graph
    2.  Per-step visual check with a confidence bar
    3.  Low confidence → ask for a better angle
    4.  Log proof frames per step
    
    **Your spin:** Lab protocols, IKEA builds, medication setup, bike repair.
    
*   Memory
    
    ### Visual memory you can text
    
    During calls, the agent indexes what it sees. Later you text “where did I leave my keys?” and it answers with when and where it last saw them.
    
    Under the hood
    
    1.  Embed sampled frames
    2.  Store with time and place in a vector DB
    3.  iMessage question → retrieval
    4.  Answer by text, or call to show it
    
    **Your spin:** Inventory for a lab or a store shelf, a home move, a closet.
    
*   Accessibility
    
    ### Walking guide for low vision
    
    The agent rides along on a call while you walk, reads signs and crossing signals, flags obstacles, and only speaks when it matters. When it’s unsure, it adds a sighted friend to the call.
    
    Under the hood
    
    1.  Stream the rear camera on a call
    2.  Detect obstacles, text and signals
    3.  Priority queue so it talks only when needed
    4.  Low confidence → add a friend to a group call
    
    **Your spin:** Grocery aisles, airports, campus buildings, reading a medicine label.
    

Questions
---------

The usual ones. Anything else, text Chert on the phone up top.

How do we get set up?

Copy the setup prompt into Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. It signs you up and connects your agent to Chert in about 5 minutes. No form needed.

Do we need to pay for anything?

No. Paste the setup prompt and your team gets a free Chert line for 48 hours.

Does my agent need a face or avatar?

No. It can be a character or no character at all. What matters is what it does with what it sees.

Can we use iMessage too?

Yes. A lot of strong builds text first, then call when they need to see something.

What do we need to bring?

At least one iPhone per team, plus the laptop you’re building on.

What do the winners get?

1st place gets $400. 1st place team gets guaranteed interviews for Chert’s FDE (forward deployed engineer) and SWE intern roles. We’re currently expanding our team and actively hiring. Chert is backed by Y Combinator (P26), OpenAI, Z Fellows and angels.

Can the agent share or control my screen?

Not yet. Today the agent sees the caller’s camera, sends video back, and joins one-to-one or group FaceTime calls.

Give your agent eyes this weekend.
----------------------------------

Paste one prompt into your coding agent. You’re on Chert in about 5 minutes.

Copy setup prompt

Stuck? Ask in the Chert Discord or find Stanley at the help desk.

![Chert](/_next/image?url=%2Fchert-lockup.png&w=256&q=75&REDACTED)[API docs](https://docs.trychert.com/introduction)
